newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia sorghum, other grains mostly quiet.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sorghum, other grains mostly quiet.

text.p: Australian sorghum export values ended the past week largely unchanged, Rob Brealey, trading manager of Queensland co-operative Grainco, said on Monday.
A slight decline in world values was offset by the Australian dollar's fall against the U.S. dollar, he said in Grainco's weekly market report.
There were no reasons for sharp short-term price fluctuations one way or the other and exchange rates were likely to be the major influencing factors this week, he said.

South Queensland sorghum values had eased slightly as harvest approached, he said. Sorghum for March/April delivery was offered late last week at A$135 a tonne Brisbane, with bids around A$130 a tonne.
Some premiums were paid in central Queensland for prompt delivery because of rain delays in accessing contracted spring harvest sorghum, he said.
Market activity in feed barley had been negligible. Grainco was offering A$142 a tonne for deliveries direct to the Brisbane Fishermans Island terminal this week.
Malting barley values were steady over the past week although deferred values continued to be pressured as Australian production of about 2.5 million tonnes moved to cover residual export demand.
The cottonseed market continued to attract interest, especially from exporters, he said.
Despite an increasing perception that the Australian crop would not be as large as initially predicted, prices continued to be talked down by export consumers, he said.

New crop seed was being bid at less than US$180 a tonne delivered Japanese port for bulk containerised seed while the majority of domestic merchants were content to offer at US$190 a tonne or better, he said.
Price direction would become clearer as harvest approached but recent rain was likely to delay the start of picking in many areas, he said.
